title: On the phone
goal: Make calls, leave messages and write texts — the final test of your Hebrew, because on the phone there's no face or hands to help you.
bekal: making a call and introducing yourself on the phone
asking the other person to repeat or slow down

dialogs.title: שִׂיחָה — שִׂיחַת טֶלֶפוֹן אַחֲרוֹנָה
dialogs.intro: Budi's last evening in Israel. He calls Noa.

lines.speaker: בּוּדִי:
lines.text: הַלּוֹ נֹעָה, זֶה בּוּדִי. אַתְּ פְּנוּיָה?
lines.baca: halo no'ah, zeh budi. at pnuyah?
lines.id: Hi Noa, it's Budi. Are you free?
lines.literal: hello noa, this budi. you (f) free?

lines.speaker: בּוּדִי:
lines.text: אֲנִי טָס מָחָר. רָצִיתִי לְהַגִּיד תּוֹדָה.
lines.baca: ani tas makhar. ratsiti lehagid todah.
lines.id: I'm flying tomorrow. I wanted to say thank you.
lines.literal: I fly tomorrow. I-want to-say thanks.

lines.speaker: בּוּדִי:
lines.text: מְאוֹד. סְלִיחָה, אֲנִי לֹא שׁוֹמֵעַ טוֹב.
lines.baca: me'od. slikhah, ani lo shome'a tov.
lines.id: Yeah. Sorry, I can't hear you very well.
lines.literal: very. sorry, I not hear well.

lines.speaker: נֹעָה:
lines.text: רֶגַע, אֲנִי יוֹצֵאת הַחוּצָה. עַכְשָׁו טוֹב?
lines.baca: rega, ani yotset hakhutsah. akhshav tov?
lines.id: One moment, I'm stepping outside. Better now?
lines.literal: moment, I go-out to-outside. now good?

lines.speaker: בּוּדִי:
lines.text: מְעֻלֶּה. תִּשְׁמְעִי — הָיָה לִי חֹדֶשׁ נִפְלָא.
lines.baca: me'uleh. tishme'i — hayah li khodesh nifla.
lines.id: Crystal clear. Listen — this month has been amazing for me.
lines.literal: excellent. listen (f) — there-was to-me month amazing.

lines.speaker: נֹעָה:
lines.id: And your Hebrew has improved so much!

lines.speaker: בּוּדִי:
lines.text: בִּזְכוּתֵךְ. אַתְּ אַף פַּעַם לֹא עָבַרְתְּ לְאַנְגְּלִית.
lines.baca: bizkhutekh. at af pa'am lo avart le'anglit.
lines.id: Thanks to you. You never once switched to English.
lines.literal: by-merit-of-you. you even-once not switched to-english.

lines.speaker: נֹעָה:
lines.text: זֶה הַכְּלָל שֶׁלִּי. תַּחֲזֹר, כֵּן? נִשָּׁאֵר בְּקֶשֶׁר.
lines.baca: zeh haklal sheli. takhazor, ken? nisha'er bekesher.
lines.id: That's my rule. You'll come back, right? Let's stay in touch.
lines.literal: this the-rule of-me. you-will-return, yes? we-will-stay in-contact.

lines.speaker: בּוּדִי:
lines.text: בְּוַדַּאי. לְהִתְרָאוֹת, נֹעָה. תּוֹדָה עַל הַכֹּל.
lines.baca: bevadai. lehitra'ot, no'ah. todah al hakol.
lines.id: Definitely. Bye, Noa. Thanks for everything.
lines.literal: with-certainty. goodbye, noa. thanks for all.

notes: **זֶה בּוּדִי** = "this is Budi" — how you introduce yourself on the phone. Hebrew doesn't say "I'm Budi" on the phone; it uses זֶה, just like English "it's Budi" or "this is Budi".
**מָה קוֹרֶה?** ("what's happening?") is a casual greeting like "what's up", very common on the phone. The answer can be as short as הַכֹּל בְּסֵדֶר.

⚠️ **On the phone you lose faces, hands and surroundings** — three things that have quietly been supporting your understanding all along. That's why phoning feels so much harder than talking face to face, and it's **not a sign your Hebrew is getting worse**. What you need isn't new vocabulary but the three lifesaver sentences in the next box.
**הִשְׁתַּפְּרָה** ("improved") is a מִתְ־ family verb in the past, with the letter swap you saw in unit 10 (מִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ). You don't need to form it yourself at A1 — just recognize it.
**בִּזְכוּתֵךְ** ("thanks to you") — from זְכוּת (merit, credit). To a man: בִּזְכוּתְךָ. A warm, understated phrase, right for thanking someone for something big.
**נִשָּׁאֵר בְּקֶשֶׁר** = "we'll stay in touch". A standard goodbye line, and in Israel it's usually meant.

⚠️ **Notice what Noa has done all through this module:** she never switched to English. That's the greatest gift a native speaker can give, and also something you need to ask for openly. The sentence: **בְּבַקָּשָׁה, דַּבֵּר אִתִּי בְּעִבְרִית** ("please, speak to me in Hebrew").
**תּוֹדָה עַל הַכֹּל** = "thanks for everything". Note עַל, not בִּשְׁבִיל — thanking in Hebrew always uses עַל.

grammars.title: Three lifesaver sentences on the phone
body: It's not vocabulary that saves you on the phone, but the ability to pause the conversation without ending it.

head: Hebrew
Say it
English
When
rows: the other person is too fast
Could you write it for me?

after: ⚠️ **תּוּכַל לִכְתֹּב לִי?** is the sentence learners underrate most. Names, addresses and numbers are the three hardest things to catch over the phone in any language — asking for them in writing isn't weakness; native speakers do it too.

grammars.title: Writing texts: Hebrew without niqqud, once more
body: Israeli WhatsApp messages are written without niqqud, often without punctuation, and full of shortcuts. Here are examples you can read right now.
after: **סַבָּבָה** and **יַאלְלָה** both come from Arabic and are now an inseparable part of everyday Hebrew. יַאלְלָה is used for "come on", "let's wrap up" and to close a conversation all at once — a bit like "OK then" in English.

blocks.title: Leaving a message
items: **שָׁלוֹם, זֶה בּוּדִי.** — hi, this is Budi.
**תַּחֲזֹר אֵלַי, בְּבַקָּשָׁה** — please call me back. To a woman: תַּחְזְרִי אֵלַי.

sections.title: How far you've come — and what's next

blocks.text: Twenty units done. Let's be honest about what that means, and what it doesn't yet.

items: **Read and write Hebrew letters** — with and without niqqud, including signs and text messages.
**Build sentences in three tenses** — past, present, future — with the most common verbs.
**Get through a full day in Israel** — ordering food, buying tickets, asking the way, going to the pharmacy, making plans, phoning.
**Talk about yourself and your day** — where you're from, family, work, activities, plans.
**Recognize three verb families** — פָּעַל, פִּעֵל and הִתְפַּעֵל — enough to guess the meaning of new verbs from their roots.

blocks.text: What you can't yet — and that's normal

items: **The other four binyanim** (נִפְעַל, הִפְעִיל, הֻפְעַל, פֻּעַל) — A2 material.
**Long complex sentences** — subordinate clauses, conditionals, reported speech.
**Native-speaker speed** — this isn't about grammar but about hours of listening, and there's no shortcut.

blocks.title: Three things that will boost your level most now
items: **Reread every dialogue in this module without niqqud.** Copy them out by hand if you need to. It's the biggest step from A1 to A2, and it needs no new material at all.
**Find one native speaker willing not to switch to English.** It's not too much to ask — the sentence בְּבַקָּשָׁה, דַּבֵּר אִתִּי בְּעִבְרִית is almost always respected.
**Listen to children's news or Israeli songs with the lyrics.** Ninety percent of the vocabulary is already in this module; all you're training is speed.

blocks.text: You started this module with twenty-two unfamiliar shapes and a reading direction that felt backwards. You finish it able to phone someone in Tel Aviv and thank them in their own language. That's no small achievement.
